reason: This passage from 2 Kings 24-25 recounts King Zedekiah's reign and the fall of Jerusalem. The text explicitly states that Zedekiah 'did evil in the eyes of the Lord' (וַיַּעַשׂ הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה) and that he rebelled against the king of Babylon (וַיִּמְרֹד צִדְקִיָּהוּ בְּמֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל). Rather than exemplifying humility in the face of criticism or correction, Zedekiah's defiance and lack of submission led to catastrophic consequences: the siege of Jerusalem, the city's fall, the execution of his sons before his eyes, his own blindness and captivity. The narrative presents Zedekiah as a negative exemplar—a cautionary tale of pride and resistance to authority—not as a model of good leadership through humility.
